  Burbank Cultural Arts Commission Meeting Minutes

  Thursday, June 11, 2026
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order at 9:01 am by Vice Chair Eric Conner.

ROLL CALL
Present  Eric Conner, Katherine Zoraster, Stefanie Girard, Cynthia Pease, Mercedes Cooper, Leah Harrison,
  James Fletcher, Jackie Brenneman (arrived at 9:05 a.m.)

Absent:  Monica Pa Moye

Staff Present:  Kristen Smith, Bryce Burton, Jocelyn Pelaez, Andrea Del Rio

Liaisons Present: Mayor Tamala Takahashi

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Mr. Burton provided an update on the current exhibit at the Betsy Lueke Creative Arts Center and shared information
about the upcoming exhibit scheduled to open in July. He also announced that tickets for the 2026 Starlight Bowl
Summer Concert Series are now on sale. Additionally, he informed the Commission of an outdoor movie event that will
take place on June 20, 2026, at Johnny Carson Park.

Ms. Pelaez provided a Beautification Program update.

Ms. Smith announced the appointment of the new Cultural Affairs Supervisor and introduced Ms. Christie Lesinski to
the Commission.

Ms. Pease provided a brief recap of the Downtown Burbank Arts Festival and reported that the event was well attended
and successful.

Ms. Girard announced that the Game of Shrooms art event will take place in Burbank this weekend and encouraged
interested individuals to participate.

Mr. Conner announced upcoming art-related events taking place in Burbank during the month of June.

ORAL COMMUNICATION
Jennifer Lorigo from the Burbank Arts and Education Foundation gave an update on upcoming events.

Mark Scroggs, a local talent agent, informed the Commission on the filming industry in Burbank.

Mayor Tamala Takahashi provided the Commission with an update on the recent budget approval for art related events
in Burbank.

REPSONSE TO ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
Ms. Pease encouraged the community to continue advocating for the arts.

Ms. Harrison thanked the City Council for the adoption of the budget and City staff for their support.

Mr. Conner commented on a recent film production that was shot in Burbank and noted that film and television
production activity is beginning to return to the area.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
None.
   FINAL
CONSENT AGENDA
APPROVAL OF MINUTES AND FINANCIAL UPDATE for May 14, 2026 - Regular Meeting Action: A motion was made by
Ms. Pease seconded by Ms. Harrison and passed 7-0 to approve May Consent Calendar. (In favor: Eric Conner, Stefanie
Girard, Cynthia Pease, Mercedes Cooper, Leah Harrison, Katherine Zoraster, James Fletcher – Abstain: Jackie
Brenneman, Absent: Monica Pa Moye).

NEW BUSINESS

  1. Community Arts Grant Program Update
  Community Arts Grant recipients presented information on their upcoming events and projects supported
  through the Community Arts Grant Program. Melonie Grasty shared information about her organization and
  an upcoming event at the Salit Conservatory funded through the grant program. Yozmit Kwon expressed
  appreciation to the Commission for the Community Arts Grant award and provided details regarding an
  upcoming project taking the streets of Burbank. Ms. Pelaez also updated the Commission with a handout of
  all the grant recipients for 2026.

  2. Fiscal Year 26/27 Budget Update
  Ms. Smith updated the Commission of the adopted Fiscal Year 2026/2027 Budget approval from City Council
  of $115,000 that was awarded to the Burbank Cultural Arts Commission to be used towards supporting
  cultural arts projects in Burbank.

  3. Consideration of Commissioner Attendance
  Ms. Smith presented the Commission with the consideration of Commissioner Brenneman's attendance and
  requested a recommendation to City Council regarding her absences. Ms. Brenneman addressed the
  Commission and explained that her absences were due to professional obligations. She noted that her work
  remained arts-related and that she continued to support and advocate for the arts during her time away
  from Commission meetings.

  Following discussion, the Commission voted to recommend that the City Council excuse Commissioner
  Brenneman's absences, recognizing her continued advocacy for the arts and her significant contributions to
  the Commission and the arts community throughout her tenure.

  Regular Meeting Action: A motion was made by Mr. Conner, seconded by Ms. Zoraster and passed 5-0 for the
  Commission to recommend to excuse Ms. Brenneman’s absences. (In favor: Eric Conner, Leah Harrison,
  Katherine Zoraster, James Fletcher, Mercedes Cooper – Abstain: Stefanie Girard, Jackie Brenneman, Cynthia
  Pease, Absent: Monica Pa Moye).

  4. Art and Business Mixer Update
  Ms. Harrison announced the upcoming Art and Business Mixer on Sunday June 14, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. at The
  Colony Theatre.

  5. 2026 Starlight Bowl Summer Concert Series
  Mr. Burton presented information regarding the Starlight Bowl concert schedule and discussed the possibility
  of the Commission hosting an informational table at an event.

  Regular Meeting Action: A motion was made by Ms. Harrison, seconded by Ms. Brenneman and passed 7-0
  for the Commission to attend the August 22, 2026, show. (In favor: Stefanie Girard, Cynthia Pease, Eric
  Conner, Leah Harrison, Katherine Zoraster, James Fletcher, Jackie Brenneman – Abstain: Mercedes Cooper
  Absent: Monica Pa Moye).

OLD BUSINESS
   1. Commission Marketing Materials  FINAL
  Ms. Pelaez proposed a selection of t-shirt designs for the Commission to evaluate as promotional
  merchandise for Burbank Arts to distribute to the public.

GOALS

  Goal 1: Capacity
  Ms. Harrison did not have an update to share with the Commission.

  Goal 2: Visibility
  Mr. Burton updated the Commission on the June schedule for the upcoming Burbank Arts website redesign
  and shared the current proposed updates.

  Goal 3: Spaces
  Ms. Zoraster did not have any updates.

  Goal 4: Advocacy
  Ms. Pease did not have any updates.

NEW AGENDA ITEMS
None.

ADJOURNMENT
The meeting was adjourned at 10:51 a.m. by Vice Chair Mr. Conner.

FROM:  Marisa Garcia,  Parks and Recreation  Director
  VIA: Erin Barrows, Recreation Services Ma  r
  BY: Christie Lesinski, Cultural Affairs Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Review of City Council Goals and Expectations of Board Members

RECOMMENDATION
Note and file.

BACKGROUND  & DISCUSSION
In 2018, City staff developed a code of conduct for all Boards, Commissions, and
Committees (BCC) members. This document, titled City Council Expectations of Board,
Commission, and Committee Members (Attachment 1) was last updated in 2022 and is
provided to all BCC members when they take the oath of office. During several meetings
in early 2025, City Council (Council) discussed potential revisions to this document.
These discussions culminated in the Council's adoption of updated City Council
Expectations of BCCs Members on March 10, 2026.

The updated document includes the following requirements:
  1. Staff should clearly communicate the City Council's goals and _ priorities
  (Attachment 2) as established during the annual City Council Goal Setting Meeting.
  2. Council Expectations shall be agendized and reviewed with members at the first
  meeting following biennial August appointments.

This report fulfills the requirement to present the updated information to the Commission
for its review and discussion. Both attachments include the updated City Council
Expectations of Board, Commission, and Committee Members and the City of Burbank
Council Priorities 2025-26. Staff will provide a brief overview of both documents during
the Cultural Arts Commission meeting.
 CONCLUSION
As an informational item only. Staff recommends that the Cultural Arts Commission note
and file the report.

ATTACHMENTS
Attachment 1 - City Council Expectations of Board, Commission, and Committee
  Members
Attachment 2 - City of Burbank Council Priorities 2025-26
   ATTACHMENT 1

  Adopted: March 10, 2026

  CITY COUNCIL EXPECTATIONS OF
  BOARD, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS

EXPECTATIONS:

    Personal agendas must be set aside, and decisions must be made in the best
  interest of the Burbank community.
    Go “through the Chair” to facilitate orderly discussion. Give all members an
  opportunity to state their opinion or position and encourage healthy deliberation
  and openness to consider all ideas.
    Work together efficiently, even when disagreements arise on an issue.
  Demonstrate respect, friendliness, and remain polite to effectively make decisions.
    Refrain from making comments that may be seen as divisive, unnecessary, or
  inappropriate.
    Avoid lengthy conversations on an agenda item once it has been voted on. If
  necessary, briefly articulate the reasoning behind your vote.
    Unanimous votes are not necessary. It is encouraged to express your personal
  opinions or positions.
    Share any relevant information and documents received from the public with
  designated City staff as soon as possible so it can be properly distributed to all
  members.
    Form connections with fellow members before, during, and after meetings, but be
  sure to do so in a manner not in violation of California’s open meeting law, the
  Brown Act.
    Members will conduct themselves within the confines of the law, including the
  Brown Act and Political Reform Act, to ensure transparency and accountability to
  members of the public.
    Members shall disclose any bias, conflicts of interest or potential conflicts of
  interest, and must recuse themselves from participating in any matter that could
  significantly impact (positively or negatively) their personal interests.
    Requests that are consistent with the duties, scope, or agenda of the Board,
  Commission, or Committee shall be made to the appropriate staff or staff liaison
  at a relevant period during the meeting. Members will not otherwise direct work to
  other department staff members.
    Once the Council has taken a position and voted on an item, it should be
  considered a non-issue for further discussion by Members, unless the item is being
  brought back to Council for review.

  1|Page
   Adopted: March 10, 2026

    Members shall not step down from the dais during meetings to speak during public
  comment on matters not appearing on the agenda and shall instead reserve any
  non-agenda comments to areas of the agenda that allow for this type of discussion
  in compliance with the Brown Act exceptions listed in Government Code section
  54954.2(a)(3).
    When presenting individual opinions and positions, members must speak only for
  themselves as an individual and explicitly state that they are presenting on their
  own behalf and are not representing the Board, Commission, or Committee, or
  other members, especially if approached by the media. Best practice is to direct
  any media inquiries to the Board, Commission, or Committee’s staff liaison.
    Members shall be responsible for conducting themselves in a professional manner
  that best represents the City when in attendance of events or gatherings outside
  of regular meetings.
    Members are encouraged to wear respectful attire at public meetings and when on
  official City business.
    Attendance: Members are expected to attend meetings on a regular basis and
  comply with the BCC Attendance Policy, as set forth in the Burbank Municipal
  Code Section 2-1-403: ABSENCES, VACANCIES, AND ADDITIONAL REASONS
  FOR REMOVAL. A summary of the policy is provided below:

  Two absences in the 12-month period from August 1 to July 31 will result in
  a written warning issued via email from City staff. The third absence may
  result in a member’s removal by Council. Should the Council excuse the
  member’s accrued absences, and the member misses an additional meeting
  within the following 12-month absence reporting period, the City Clerk may
  proceed with the member’s automatic removal by City staff.

  Violation of these expectations may result in a member’s dismissal.

COUNCIL EXPECTATIONS OF THE CHAIR/VICE CHAIR:

    The Chair should work with City staff to ensure that agenda topics are within the
  scope of the Board, Commission, or Committee’s mission, have a clear purpose,
  and align with the City Council’s goals.

    The Chair and Vice Chair shall work with City staff to receive training on how to
  effectively facilitate a meeting.

    The Chair should meet with City staff as needed to discuss matters related to
  conduct of the meeting.

    The Chair shall apply a two-hour initial time limit to meetings. In the event that a
  meeting may exceed two hours, the Chair shall confer with the staff liaison to

  2|Page
   Adopted: March 10, 2026

  review the status of the remaining items and determine the best manner to
  proceed.

    The Chair shall follow City Council meeting guidelines where applicable (e.g.,
  guidelines for respectful engagement, public comment speaking time limits, etc.).

COUNCIL EXPECTATIONS OF CITY STAFF:

    Staff should clearly communicate the City Council’s goals and priorities as
  established during the annual City Council Goal Setting Meeting.

    Staff should assist the Chair with conducting the meeting in an efficient and
  effective manner and advise regarding proceeding with the Board, Commission,
  and Committee’s business in accordance with the Brown Act.

    Council Expectations shall be agendized and reviewed with Members at the first
  meeting following biennial August appointments.

    Reports and presentations on agenda items will provide an objective analysis on
  the issue and will not favor a particular point of view. Alternatives and options on
  item actions should be presented.

    Staff will remain impartial and strive to maintain cooperative and supportive
  relationships with all members, regardless of any differences in opinion that may
  exist or arise.

    Staff will take requests from the Board, Commission, or Committee as a body, and
  not from individual members, if such request is relevant to the duties, scope or
  agenda of the Board, Commission, or Committee.

    Staff will work with the Board, Commission, or Committee to obtain a vote on
  advisory matters being presented to the City Council.

City of Burbank
Council Priorities 2025-26
  City Services
  Support efforts to ensure the City is a top-rated employer,
  maintain and enhance the City’s financial health, develop and
  enhance streamlined approaches to online services and
  applications, evaluate and enhance the 311 app, and
  collaborate with community partners and the school district.

  Economic Development
  Support long term prosperity, stability, and opportunity by
  diversifying the City’s economic base, supporting media and
  industry companies, and continuing to attract and retain
  high quality businesses. Focus on the completion of various
  specific plans in the City and engage in preparation for large
  scale events, such as the 2028 Olympics, and anticipated
  2026 opening of the replacement passenger terminal at
  Hollywood Burbank Airport (Elevate BUR).

  Housing
  Facilitate the increased supply of housing. Encourage
  options such as mixed-use developments and rezoning of
  vacant commercial properties. Implement the Housing
  Enforcement Program and continue to explore tenant
  protections. Continue to collaborate with community
  partners in addressing and reducing homelessness.

  Public Safety
  Prioritize public safety through programs and initiatives that
  assist internal safety departments and the community
  prepare for a major disaster. Maintain appropriate levels of
  police and fire personnel and support services provided by
  the Mental Health Evaluation Team and Community Service
  Officers.

  Quality of Life
  Support Burbank’s strong sense of community, well-
  maintained public services, and vibrant cultural scene.
  Provide and enhance the City’s community spaces and
  events, artistic and creative endeavors, and access to vital
  city services.

  Sustainability
  Enhance sustainable practices, including increased usage of
  solar power and additional electrification requirements.
  Support innovative measures to conserve water and power,
  enhance the City’s tree canopy, and combat the effects of
  urban heat. Develop policies that support electrification and
  high air quality.

  Transportation/Traffic
  Encourage integration and enhancement of transportation
  solutions related to auto, bus, and rail. Consider new modes
  of transportation while enhancing the community’s access
  to safe bike and walking paths. Continue to evaluate
  parking availability and solutions within the City.

   Priority Action Plan
  2025-26
  CITY SERVICES
  1) Recruit and retain high caliber employees, 2) Maintain a balanced general fund budget, 3) Develop long term ﬁnancial goals,
  4) Streamline/standardize online applications, 5) Prioritize information accessibility, 6) Maintain and enhance the 311 app, and
  7) Collaborate with community partners and school district.

  A  Maintain the City's status as a top rated employer by negotiating new contracts with labor groups in alignment with Council's
  compensation policy, creating a comprehensive marketing plan to showcase the City as an employer, implementing AB 2561
  related to providing Council with the City's employment vacancy rate, and providing employees with ongoing training
